residueAnswer.theGuard: UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL: cell_state = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.kind = 'unaccounted' AND stored.kind <> 'unaccounted' THEN stored ELSE EXCLUDED END. Only unaccounted is refused.
residueAnswer.mayACrosswalkValueReplaceAStoredJoinMiss: YES, and it is the intended repair rather than a guard violation: the guard stops DOWNGRADES, it does not freeze a wrong claim. P-310's stored absences (25,743 per money rail, 26,043 per situs-city rail, 95,384 on exemptionCodes) are exactly the cells the pair's values repair, because the field the cell calls verified-absent is present on the county's own roll for the parcel's published account.
whatAnApplyWouldDo: 282,219 bound nodes: the record is re-instantiated from the 2026 numeric account row merged with the node's own R row. A rail the account carries becomes a value (replacing a stored absence); a rail both rows are silent on becomes absent-verified citing the account's taxYear 2026 (replacing a 2025-based absence with a correct one). No bare-number fallback exists anywhere on this path.
73 situs-recovered residue nodes: the same shape, from the situs-resolved account row.
350 unreached nodes: unaccounted, which the guard REFUSES over their stored cells. They keep their old claim, counted (railsUncleared) and never silently left as truth.
a stored value is never touched by an incoming unaccounted, so no rail can be emptied by this change.

p351Answer.question: does the bake's retirement arm (LDT nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts, buildConformantTier1Payload) need this same pair to stop retiring Williamson's live parcels, and in which direction?
p351Answer.answer: YES -- the same pair, used from the same side: NODE (R account) -> published pair -> NUMERIC account -> byPropId lookup.
p351Answer.fromTheCode: apn = the served node's own prop_id (for 48491, R-prefixed); fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll loads cad_property WHERE tax_year = the declared vintage (48491 -> 2026, cad-export) and keys byPropId; recordRetirement = apn != null && cadPropConsulted && byPropId.get(apn) == null.

threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesTheLoaderAndTheBind: For county 48491, `loadLandingAndCad` takes its pair branch FIRST: `assertSeedKeyPopulation` (census/refusal) -> `loadPublishedWcadPair` (WCAD_PAIR_CTES + WILLIAMSON_WCAD_PAIR_SQL: per-extract partition-unique ambiguity guard, cross-extract corroborator, `kept`) -> `loadWilliamsonUnboundNodeIds` (same CTEs, county-wide) -> `loadWilliamsonSitusFallback` (the existing WILLIAMSON_CROSSWALK_SQL over the unbound residue, once per run) -> `loadWilliamsonNodeRollRows` + `loadWilliamsonPairAccountRows` (batched for the page's keys) -> `mergeWilliamsonPairRow` (add-only: the node's own R row wins field-by-field, the account fills what it is silent on, tax_year+prop_id come from the account). The merged row is handed to `instantiateAndIngest`, whose vendored engine (`applyCadScalar`/`cadNullVerified`) stamps the cells, and `upsertRecords` writes them under UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL's guard, restricted to FILL_OWNED_RAIL_KEYS.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersThem: Any run of the parcel-record-fill job for 48491 -- `fillCountyWide` per page, or `runParcelRecordFill` county-wide (the writer job's own CLI/cron path). There is no event, no queue and no upstream stage gate: the trigger is the run, and each run re-reads the pair (once per process) and the key census, so a roll change or a key-population change is picked up by the next run rather than needing a deploy. Precondition: the two published extracts are populated (the acquisition jobs keep them current); nothing else.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenThePairIsAmbiguousOrStale: AMBIGUOUS: a duplicated quickrefid or propertyid inside either extract is dropped from that extract's clean set in BOTH directions, and a pair the two extracts contradict is refused for both -- so the affected nodes get NO entry, come out unaccounted (P-325) and appear as a residue jump in `joinMissUnresolved`, while `pairCensus.pairsKept` (294,399 today) names the size of the pair actually used. The guard can only ever shrink the bind into the residue, never fabricate one. STALE: it cannot be, in the sense the dispatch worries about -- the pair is re-read every run and nothing persists it, and the run record carries each extract's source_vintage/ingested_at so a bind names the roll it came from. A pair that legitimately re-points shows up as a different account for the node, and because the merge is add-only over the node's own R row, a re-point cannot drop a field the R row carries; the numeric account's values replace them.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesThem: (1) A raw SQL write into parcel_record_cell -- the bypass every writer in this repo documents, and the reason a stale or wrong stored cell cannot be cleared by any run. (2) The key population coming alive: if geo_id or property_number is ever populated, this lane's refusal fires (SEED_KEY_POPULATION_APPEARED) and the county STOPS rather than sharing its nodes between two published binders -- i.e. the guard changes behaviour before the binder does. (3) ENGINE_PIN: the vendored engine decides how a null versus a missing field is stamped (absent-verified vs unaccounted), so an engine bump can change what this bind means without touching this file, and this file may not hand-edit it. (4) Other writers on the same rails (parcel-owner.mjs follows the same convention; the guarantee is per-writer, not structural). (5) An operator/sweep write, which is exactly why the residue is counted for one rather than cleared.

fleetMemory.LESSON: A guard's DIRECTION decides which half of a population can be harmed. UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL refuses one incoming state (unaccounted) and applies everything else, so 'how many cells could move' must be split into nodes the bind RESOLVES (where an absence can overwrite a value) and nodes it leaves alone (where an unaccounted emission is refused by construction). One number over both classes is either an alarm or a false comfort, and this writer's own census produces exactly that number if you do not split it.

A published identifier pair and an address heuristic disagree on a measurable 0.019% of accounts, and the disagreement is where every remaining risk in this bind lives. Whichever one you rank first, the OTHER one is the place to look for what your change will move -- so compute the divergence set and name it on the run, even when it is 48 of 256,752.

A field census of both keyspaces (what each row actually carries) turns 'would this bind drop a value?' from an argument into arithmetic: the R slice carries land_acres on 282,569 of 282,569 rows while the numeric row it binds to carries it on 105,691 of 319,480, so binding straight to the numeric row would have moved acreage on ~189,000 parcels. That is why the merge is add-only.
fleetMemory.DEAD-END: Do not run a heavy county-wide join inside one READ ONLY transaction on a Neon POOLER hostname -- it is cancelled with 57014 (the same query standalone on the pooler finishes, and the pooler and the direct host are one lease key, so the direct hostname is both faster and equally serialized). Do not let a failed heavy statement abort the transaction that carries your other measurements: wrap the optional leg in a SAVEPOINT and mark the bound PARTIAL. Do not `process.exit()` on Windows while pg handles are closing (libuv assertion, lost exit code). Do not trust PowerShell `>` to write JSON (UTF-16).
